Relative positions here are read off published plans and aerial views by eye, not measured.

Nine platforms, the lower six square and the upper three circular, with seventy-two small stupas around one large central stupa (Wikipedia, Borobudur). The six square platforms are a `Ziggurat`; the three circular ones and the 72 stupas are `Dome`s on `arrangeOn` circles. The setback per terrace is uncited -- no source read gives it -- and is derived from the base divided by the terrace count.

The three stupa rings sit at 18, 13 and 8 m from the centre. The first attempt used 36, 26 and 16 m, which is wider than the sixth terrace: 123 m base less five 8 m setbacks leaves 21.5 m of half-width, so two of the three rings hung in the air.

SIXTEEN, TWELVE AND EIGHT STUPAS, NOT 32/24/16, and the real number is 72. At 0.5 studs/m a ring of radius 18 m is 9 studs, a circumference of 57 studs, and 32 two-stud stupas on it overlap their neighbours. The count on screen is the count that fits; the real 72 is in this note and not in the model.

The innermost ring stands 13 m out and the central stupa is 4 m: at 8 m and 6.5 m the ring ran through the stupa, eight overlaps that no plan view shows because they are the same eight studs at two heights.
